brief: wp-execute v1.0.0 — Governed execution of one work package — bind, red, green, refactor, gate, seal.

macros.title: Bind
macros.instructions:
## Phase: BIND

Read the work-package card supplied as initial_context for this session —
it carries the WP id, intent, source requirements, and acceptance
scenarios. Before touching any file, ground the session in that card.

### Your Approach:
1. Restate the WP's intent in ONE sentence — if you cannot, the card is
   ambiguous and you must stop rather than guess.
2. List every acceptance scenario (SCN id) this WP must satisfy. Do not
   invent scenarios the card does not carry; do not drop any it does.
3. Declare the surface you will touch — files and modules — BEFORE
   writing anything. This declaration is the contract for RED and GREEN.

### Rules:
- Anything outside the declared surface is scope creep. If the WP turns
  out to need more surface once work is underway, record it as an
  explicit deviation — never expand silently.
- If the card is missing intent, source requirements, or acceptance
  scenarios, STOP. An underspecified WP cannot be bound, and proceeding
  on a guess only pushes the ambiguity downstream where it is more
  expensive to catch.

### Output:
A one-sentence intent restatement, the full list of SCN ids in scope,
and the declared file/module surface.

macros.title: Red
macros.instructions:
## Phase: RED

Write the test(s) for this WP BEFORE any implementation exists. Each
test maps to exactly one acceptance scenario declared at BIND — no
test without a scenario, no scenario without a test.

### Your Approach:
1. Write the failing test(s) first. Do not write a line of
   implementation in this phase — not even a stub that happens to pass.
2. Run the tests and CAPTURE the failing output verbatim. This output
   is the evidence the gate checks; paraphrasing it is not sufficient.
3. Confirm each test fails for the RIGHT reason — a missing behavior,
   not a typo or a broken harness.

### Rules:
- A test that passes before implementation tests nothing: either the
  behavior already exists (the WP may be redundant) or the test is
  vacuous (it asserts nothing meaningful). Either case means STOP and
  rethink the test, not proceed to GREEN.
- Keep the failing output verbatim — do not summarize it away.

### Output:
The new test file(s)/cases, the scenario each maps to, and the
captured failing test-run output.

macros.title: Green
macros.instructions:
## Phase: GREEN

Write the MINIMUM implementation that makes the RED tests pass. This
phase exists to satisfy the tests already written — not to anticipate
future needs.

### Your Approach:
1. Implement only what the failing tests demand. Resist generalization
   the tests do not require — speculative flexibility is scope creep,
   the same as touching undeclared files.
2. Run the tests and capture the passing output verbatim.
3. Stay inside the surface declared at BIND.

### Rules:
- If you must leave the declared surface to make the tests pass, record
  the deviation explicitly — do not expand the surface silently.
- Do not refactor here. REFACTOR is a separate, predicate-gated phase.

### Output:
The minimal implementation change(s), the captured passing test-run
output, and a note confirming the declared surface was respected (or an
explicit deviation record if not).

macros.title: Refactor
macros.instructions:
## Phase: REFACTOR

Refactor is predicate-gated, not automatic. Check the triggers before
touching anything:
- duplicated logic introduced during GREEN
- a function or file that has outgrown its module's norms
- naming that no longer reflects behavior

### Your Approach:
1. Evaluate each trigger against the GREEN diff. If NONE fires, record
   "no refactor needed" with one line of justification — skipping
   honestly is compliant, skipping silently is not.
2. If a trigger fires, refactor with tests green the whole time — run
   them after every change, not just at the end.
3. Behavior must not change. The tests are the ratchet: if a test needs
   to change to keep passing, that is not a refactor, it is new
   behavior, and it belongs in a new RED/GREEN cycle.

### Output:
Either the refactor diff with tests green throughout, or the recorded
"no refactor needed" justification.

macros.title: Verification Gate
macros.instructions:
## Phase: VERIFICATION GATE

This is full verification, not just a re-run of the WP's own tests.

### Your Approach:
1. Run the ENTIRE project test suite — a WP that breaks a neighbor is
   not done, even if its own tests are green.
2. Run the linter/formatter checks the project uses.
3. Walk the acceptance scenarios from BIND one by one and record
   pass/fail per SCN id — do not summarize this as a single verdict.
4. Capture command outputs as evidence for every check above.

### Rules:
- Any single failure — suite, lint, or scenario — means this gate does
  not pass. Fix and re-run the full set; do not cherry-pick a re-run of
  only the failing piece.
- The cold-review step that follows is a skeptic's pass over this
  evidence: it checks that every claimed pass has captured output, and
  that each check would actually fail if the code were wrong.

### Output:
Full-suite output, lint output, and a per-SCN-id pass/fail table.

macros.title: Seal
macros.instructions:
## Phase: SEAL

Assemble the seal record — the final JSON deliverable the profile's
output_contract validates.

### Your Approach:
1. wp_id and intent — carried from the WP card bound at BIND.
2. outputs — the artifacts actually produced (file paths).
3. provenance — the commands run in this session with their evidence;
   every entry must correspond to a command actually executed here,
   never a plausible-sounding placeholder.
4. acceptance_results — one entry per SCN id from the verification
   gate, each with its pass/fail result.
5. assurance_level — "floor" (tests only), "property" (property-based
   tests included), or "full" (tests + property + external
   verification). Choose honestly based on what this session actually
   ran.

### Rules:
- The seal is a claim you sign with evidence. Do not record an output,
  a provenance entry, or a pass you cannot back with something that
  actually happened in this session.

### Output:
The complete seal record matching the output_contract schema.

work_packages.title: Bind scope
work_packages.instructions: Restate WP intent, list acceptance scenarios, declare the surface to be touched.

work_packages.title: Bind gate
work_packages.instructions: Mechanical check that the WP is bound before any test or code is written.

work_packages.title: Write failing tests
work_packages.instructions: Author test(s) mapped to acceptance scenarios and capture the failing run.

checklist.assert: this state changed the test file
checklist.cmd: git diff --name-only ${base_ref} -- ${test_path} | grep -q . || git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- ${test_path} | grep -q .

work_packages.title: Red gate
work_packages.instructions: Mechanical check that tests were written first and genuinely fail.

checklist.cmd: python3 -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(open('${wp_dir}/bind.json'));sys.exit(0 if all(any(s.get('test') in open('${test_path}').read() for _ in [0]) for s in (d.get('scenarios') or [])) else 1)"

work_packages.title: Implement minimally
work_packages.instructions: Write the smallest implementation that turns the red tests green.

checklist.assert: this state changed the source file
checklist.cmd: git diff --name-only ${base_ref} -- ${src_path} | grep -q . || git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- ${src_path} | grep -q .

work_packages.title: Green gate
work_packages.instructions: Mechanical check that tests pass and the declared surface was respected.

work_packages.title: Refactor or record skip
work_packages.instructions: Fire the refactor triggers or record an honest skip justification.

checklist.assert: this state recorded a decision, refactor or honest skip

work_packages.title: Refactor gate
work_packages.instructions: Mechanical check that a refactor decision was recorded and tests still pass.

work_packages.title: Run full verification
work_packages.instructions: Run the full test suite, lints, and walk acceptance scenarios per SCN id.

checklist.assert: this state captured the full-suite evidence

work_packages.title: Cold-review verification
work_packages.instructions: Review the evidence as a skeptic: does every claimed pass have captured output? Would each check actually fail if the code were wrong? Verdict APPROVE or FIXES-NEEDED.

checklist.assert: the review carries at least 40 words

checklist.judge: Does this review describe the change in the diff? FAIL if it makes claims the diff does not support, if it is generic enough to apply to any change, or if it omits a material part of the diff.

work_packages.title: Verification gate
work_packages.instructions: Mechanical check that the full suite is green, lints are clean, and every scenario was walked.

checklist.cmd: python3 -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(open('${wp_dir}/verify.json'));sys.exit(0 if len(d.get('acceptance') or [])>0 and all(a.get('result')=='pass' for a in d['acceptance']) else 1)"

checklist.assert: this state assembled the seal record

work_packages.title: Seal gate
work_packages.instructions: Mechanical check that outputs, provenance, and acceptance results are all recorded.
